rationale: Both are rigorously grounded, cross-validating several of the same real issues (sync-heavy .item() calls, dead SkipSoftmaxSpec.enabled, unsupported '<2%' doc claim). Y aligns more closely with the PR's actual resolution history — it correctly recognizes the P2 SAGE-disable bug is already fixed via the trim loop, finds the AllGather-KV reject in layer.py and asks for the exact test/clarification the maintainers actually discussed, and adds a genuinely novel, concrete finding (new CPU-only tests deselected by the cuda-only pytestmark in the merge CI lane) that neither the ground truth nor X catches. X compensates with a strong, unique test-gap catch tied to the skip-softmax timestep fix mentioned in the ground truth, but several of its 'required' findings (sync overhead, unvalidated max_seqlen) are speculative perf nitpicks not raised by real reviewers, and its critique of the AllGather-KV reject as 'unrelated scope' cuts against the maintainer's endorsed deferral.
